title: Pearson PTE Academic
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public PTE Academic syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A museum guide explains that visitors may photograph exhibits without flash but must leave large bags in the free lockers near the entrance. According to the guide, what must visitors do with large bags?
options: Leave them in the free lockers near the entrance
Hand them to a security officer
Store them in a paid cloakroom
items.explanation: The guide directs visitors to leave large bags in the free lockers near the entrance, so carrying them or paying for storage contradicts the text.

items.stem: A town council notice states that recycling collection moves from weekly to fortnightly from 1 March, while garden waste collection continues weekly. How often will recycling be collected from 1 March?
items.explanation: The notice says recycling moves from weekly to fortnightly, so fortnightly is correct while garden waste alone stays weekly.

items.stem: A science article reports that city temperatures can be 5 degrees higher than the surrounding countryside because dark surfaces absorb heat, a phenomenon called the urban heat island. What effect does the article describe?
options: Higher city temperatures than the countryside
items.explanation: The article attributes higher city temperatures to dark surfaces absorbing heat, so the urban heat island is the warming of cities above rural levels.

items.stem: A passage on sleep explains that the brain consolidates new memories during deep sleep, moving information from short-term to long-term storage. What does the passage say deep sleep does?
options: Helps move memories into long-term storage
items.explanation: The passage states that deep sleep consolidates memories from short-term into long-term storage, so erasing memories or removing the need for sleep misstates it.

items.stem: A business profile notes that the firm grew quickly by acquiring smaller rivals, but analysts warn that integrating so many different company cultures may prove difficult. What concern do the analysts raise?
options: Integrating different company cultures may be difficult
The firm is too small to survive
items.explanation: The analysts warn that integrating many different cultures may be hard, so the concern is cultural integration rather than size or profit.

items.stem: A geography text explains that rivers meander because faster water on the outer bend erodes the bank while slower water on the inner bend deposits sediment. What causes a river to meander according to the text?
options: Uniform water speed across the channel
Erosion on the outer bend and deposition on the inner bend
The presence of fish in the water
items.explanation: The text balances erosion on the outer bend with deposition on the inner bend, which together create the meander pattern.

items.stem: A news report says the new rail link will cut the journey between the two cities from three hours to ninety minutes. What will be the new journey time?
items.explanation: The report gives the new journey time as ninety minutes, down from the original three hours.

items.stem: A review of a novel notes that the plot is gripping but the characters feel underdeveloped, so readers may finish it quickly without remembering anyone. What is the reviewer's overall view?
options: The plot is weak but the characters are superb
Both the plot and the characters are excellent
Both the plot and the characters are dull
The plot is gripping but the characters are underdeveloped
items.explanation: The reviewer praises the gripping plot while criticising the underdeveloped characters, so the view combines the two judgements.

items.stem: A health leaflet states that to reduce the risk of illness, hands should be washed for at least twenty seconds with soap and running water. For how long does the leaflet advise washing hands?
items.explanation: The leaflet specifies at least twenty seconds with soap and running water, so the shorter and longer alternatives are unsupported.

items.stem: A passage argues that remote work reduces commuting time yet can blur the boundary between work and home life. What does the writer identify as a disadvantage of remote work?
options: A blurred boundary between work and home
items.explanation: The writer names the blurred boundary between work and home as the drawback, while shorter commuting is presented as a benefit.

items.stem: An article on volcanoes explains that eruptions are driven by pressure from dissolved gases in magma, which expands as it rises towards the surface. What drives a volcanic eruption according to the article?
options: The weight of rainwater on the crater
Pressure from dissolved gases expanding in rising magma
items.explanation: The article identifies expanding dissolved gases in rising magma as the driving pressure, so the other options are unrelated to the process.

items.stem: A university handbook states that to pass a module a student must achieve at least 40 per cent overall and submit every required assessment. What is the minimum overall mark to pass a module?
items.explanation: The handbook sets the minimum pass mark at 40 per cent, provided that all required assessments are submitted.

items.stem: A text about bees explains that when a scout finds rich food it performs a waggle dance whose angle shows direction and whose duration shows distance. What does the duration of the dance indicate?
items.explanation: The text links the dance angle to direction and its duration to distance, so duration indicates how far away the food is.

items.stem: A report on literacy notes that children who read for pleasure daily score higher in vocabulary tests than those who rarely read. According to the report, which children score higher in vocabulary?
options: Those who read for pleasure daily
Those who read only at school
items.explanation: The report ties higher vocabulary scores to daily reading for pleasure, contrasting with children who rarely read.

items.stem: A passage describes how a desalination plant removes salt from seawater by forcing it through a membrane under high pressure. What does the plant do to seawater?
items.explanation: The passage says desalination removes salt by forcing water through a membrane, so adding salt or freezing it is incorrect.

items.stem: A travel article warns that the mountain path is closed in winter because of ice, but remains open for guided walks in summer. When does the article say the path is closed?
items.explanation: The article closes the path in winter because of ice while noting that guided walks run in summer.

items.stem: A psychology passage explains that people tend to overestimate how much others notice their mistakes, an effect known as the spotlight effect. What does the spotlight effect describe?
options: A tendency to overestimate how much others notice our mistakes
A belief that others are watching us favourably
items.explanation: The passage defines the spotlight effect as overestimating how much others notice our mistakes, not a fear of light.

items.stem: A report states that switching to LED street lighting cut the town's lighting energy use by 60 per cent. By how much did energy use for lighting fall?
items.explanation: The report gives the reduction as 60 per cent, so the other figures misread the amount stated in the text.

items.stem: A passage notes that although the internet makes information easy to find, readers must judge whether a source is reliable before trusting it. What does the writer advise readers to do?
options: Judge whether a source is reliable
items.explanation: The writer urges readers to judge a source's reliability before trusting it, rather than trusting everything or avoiding the internet.

items.stem: An archaeology text explains that carbon dating estimates an object's age by measuring how much radioactive carbon it still contains. What does carbon dating estimate?
items.explanation: The text says carbon dating estimates age from the radioactive carbon that remains, so weight, colour and value are not measured.

items.stem: In a campus audio guide a speaker says the main library is closed on Sundays but opens from eight in the morning to ten at night on other days. When is the main library closed?
items.explanation: The guide closes the library on Sundays, while other days run from eight in the morning to ten at night.

items.stem: A lecturer states that although the experiment produced the expected result, the small sample means the finding should be treated as preliminary. How does the lecturer describe the finding?
options: Preliminary and in need of more evidence
items.explanation: The lecturer cautions that the small sample makes the result preliminary, so it is not presented as final proof.

items.stem: In a recorded interview a manager says the team missed the deadline because a key supplier delivered parts two weeks late. Why did the team miss the deadline?
options: The team took too many breaks
items.explanation: The manager blames a supplier that delivered two weeks late, so the other causes are not given in the recording.

items.stem: A radio feature reports that the city's new tram line carried one million passengers in its first year, twice the original forecast. How many passengers did the tram line carry in its first year?
items.explanation: The feature states one million passengers, which was twice the forecast rather than an actual figure of two million.

items.stem: In a lecture a speaker says the human body replaces most of its cells over time, so the body you have now is not made of exactly the same material as years ago. What does the speaker claim about the body's cells?
options: They are identical to a machine's parts
items.explanation: The speaker says most cells are replaced over time, meaning the body's material changes rather than staying fixed.

items.stem: A campus announcement explains that the careers fair moves from the main hall to the sports centre because more employers are attending than expected. Where will the careers fair be held?
items.explanation: The announcement relocates the fair to the sports centre because of the larger number of employers expected.

items.stem: In a voicemail a colleague says the morning meeting is cancelled but the afternoon review will go ahead as planned. Which meeting is cancelled?
items.explanation: The voicemail cancels the morning meeting yet keeps the afternoon review, so only the morning one is cancelled.

items.stem: A documentary narrator explains that the desert blooms briefly after heavy rain because dormant seeds germinate once they absorb enough water. What causes the desert to bloom?
items.explanation: The narrator ties the bloom to heavy rain that lets dormant seeds germinate, so temperature and wind are not the cause.

items.stem: A lecturer says the printing press lowered the cost of books so dramatically that literacy spread far more widely within a single generation. What effect does the lecturer attribute to the printing press?
options: It lowered book costs and spread literacy
It reduced the number of readers
items.explanation: The lecturer says cheaper books helped literacy spread widely, which is the effect named in the recording.

items.stem: In a phone message a travel agent confirms a flight has been rescheduled from Tuesday to Wednesday and that the change is free of charge. To which day has the flight moved?
items.explanation: The agent moves the flight from Tuesday to Wednesday and waives the fee, so Wednesday is the new day.

items.stem: A lecturer explains that inflation measures the rate at which the general level of prices rises over time, reducing what a given amount of money can buy. What does inflation measure?
options: The fall in prices over time
The rise in the general price level
items.explanation: The lecturer defines inflation as the rising general price level, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

items.stem: A recorded safety briefing states that in an emergency staff should leave by the nearest exit and gather at the assembly point on the north lawn. Where should staff gather?
items.explanation: The briefing directs staff to the assembly point on the north lawn after leaving by the nearest exit.

items.stem: A narrator says the marathon route was changed this year to avoid roadworks and now passes along the river. Why was the route changed?
options: To reduce the number of runners
items.explanation: The narrator says the route was altered to avoid roadworks, and it now runs along the river.

items.stem: In a tutorial recording the student admits the data set is incomplete and the tutor suggests repeating the survey with a larger group. What does the tutor suggest?
options: Repeating the survey with a larger group
items.explanation: The tutor responds to the incomplete data by suggesting a repeat survey with a larger group, not abandonment.

items.stem: A news bulletin reports that the museum will return a set of artefacts to their country of origin following a long negotiation. What will the museum do?
options: Return artefacts to their country of origin
items.explanation: The bulletin says the artefacts will be returned to their country of origin after negotiation, so the other actions are wrong.

items.stem: A lecturer explains that compound interest earns interest on both the original sum and the interest already earned, so savings grow faster over time. On what does compound interest earn interest?
options: Both the original sum and accumulated interest
items.explanation: The lecturer says compound interest applies to the original sum plus interest already earned, which speeds up growth.

items.stem: In a recorded lecture the speaker says that coral bleaching happens when water stays too warm for too long and the coral expels the algae that feed it. What causes coral bleaching?
options: Water that stays too warm for too long
Too much salt in the water
items.explanation: The speaker links bleaching to prolonged warm water that makes coral expel its algae, so salt and shade are not the cause.

items.stem: A campus guide says the student health centre offers free flu vaccinations each October and that appointments can be booked online. When are flu vaccinations offered?
items.explanation: The guide says vaccinations are offered each October and booked online, so the other times are unsupported.

items.stem: A speaker explains that a glacier retreats when melting at its lower end exceeds the snow added at the top. When does a glacier retreat?
options: When the snow added exceeds melting
When melting exceeds the snow added
items.explanation: The speaker says a glacier retreats when melting at the lower end outpaces the snow gained at the top.

items.stem: In a recorded discussion the presenter says the company reduced waste by redesigning packaging, cutting material use by a third. By how much did material use fall?
items.explanation: The presenter says redesigning packaging cut material use by a third, so the other fractions misread the amount.

items.stem: Choose the option that completes the sentence correctly. The scientists have been studying the reef since 2018 and have published three reports, so the underlined word in this rewritten sentence shows which relationship?
options: A starting point in time for an action that continues
A length of time measured in hours
A repetition that has now stopped
A future plan that is not yet decided
items.explanation: Since introduces the point in time when a continuing action began, whereas a period would use for and a closed past would use a past tense.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. The two theories are often confused, but a careful reader can distinguish between them. Which meaning does the completed word carry?
options: To hand something out to a group
To tell two things apart clearly
To reject an idea as unimportant
items.explanation: To distinguish is to tell two things apart, while distribute, dismiss and display carry quite different meanings.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. If the sample had been larger, the results would have been more reliable. Which grammatical structure is used here?
options: A first conditional about a likely future
A present simple statement of fact
A third conditional about an unreal past situation
items.explanation: The pattern if plus past perfect with would have is a third conditional describing an unreal past, so the other descriptions do not fit.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word. The evidence was described as scant, so the committee asked for further research. What does scant mean here?
items.explanation: Scant means barely enough, which explains why more research was requested, not convincing, recent or secret.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that completes the sentence correctly. Neither the lecturer nor the students were satisfied with the new timetable. Which rule explains the verb form were?
options: With neither and nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject
The verb always takes a plural form after neither
The verb agrees with the first subject only
The verb is fixed and never changes with the subject
items.explanation: In a neither and nor construction the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is the plural students, so were is correct.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The report, together with its appendices, was submitted before the deadline. Why is the verb was singular here?
options: The subject is the plural appendices
The subject is the singular report and the added phrase does not change its number
The verb always agrees with the most recent noun
The past tense is always singular in every sentence
items.explanation: The true subject is the singular report, and the phrase together with its appendices does not change its number, so was is correct.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. The manager asked the team to revise the proposal before the board meeting. What does the completed word mean?
options: To bring something back to life
To turn something the opposite way
To review and improve a document
To move in a circle around a point
items.explanation: To revise a proposal is to review and improve it, while revive, reverse and revolve have unrelated meanings.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that completes the sentence correctly. By the time the results are published, the team will have repeated the experiment three times. Which tense is required and why?
options: The simple present, for a regular habit
The past continuous, for an interrupted action
The present perfect, for an experience with no time given
The future perfect, for an action finished before a future point
items.explanation: The future perfect describes an action completed before a stated future point, which matches the by the time clause.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word. The committee reached a unanimous decision, so no member objected. What does unanimous mean?
items.explanation: Unanimous means agreed by everyone, which is why no member objected, rather than divided, delayed or secret.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The new bridge is far wider than the old one, so traffic moves more quickly. Why is wider rather than wide correct here?
options: It is a superlative form, which is needed before than
It is a comparative form, which is needed before than
It is an adverb, which is needed before than
It is a noun, which is needed before than
items.explanation: A comparative adjective is required before than, so wider is correct, while the base, superlative and adverb forms do not fit.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that completes the sentence correctly. The researchers insisted that the data be checked by an independent team. Which construction is used after insisted?
options: The infinitive to be without a subject
items.explanation: After verbs of demand such as insist, the subjunctive base form be is standard, while was and the other forms do not fit.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. Poor maintenance can shorten the life of a machine and lead to early failure. Which form of the word is needed?
items.explanation: The sentence needs the verb shorten after the modal can, while shortness, short and shorten to do not fit that position.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. She has lived in three countries since she graduated. Why is since correct rather than for?
options: Because since marks a starting point while for marks a length of time
Because since is always used with the past simple
Because for can never be used with the present perfect
Because since is only used with future plans
items.explanation: Since introduces the point in time when something started, whereas for measures a period, so since fits graduated as a starting point.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word. The instructions were ambiguous, so several students interpreted them differently. What does ambiguous mean?
options: Open to more than one interpretation
items.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation, which explains why students understood the instructions differently.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that completes the sentence correctly. Hardly had the lecture begun when the fire alarm sounded. Which word completes the inverted structure after hardly?
options: has, because the action is recent
did, because the main verb is begin
had, because the past perfect follows hardly in this fixed pattern
was, because the sentence is passive
items.explanation: The pattern hardly plus past perfect plus when requires had, so has, did and was do not complete the structure.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. The two departments must coordinate their efforts if the project is to finish on time. What does the completed word mean?
options: Happen at the same time by chance
Mix two things up by mistake
Organise people or activities so they work well together
items.explanation: To coordinate is to organise activities so they work together, while coincide, confuse and confine do not express that idea.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The ancient manuscript is so fragile that it must be handled only with gloves. Why is must correct here?
options: It expresses a requirement or rule
items.explanation: The modal must states a requirement or rule, whereas the other options describe habits, questions or intentions that do not fit.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word. The findings were consistent with earlier studies, so the team was reassured. What does consistent with mean here?
items.explanation: Consistent with means in agreement with, which is why the team felt reassured rather than alarmed or surprised.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that completes the sentence correctly. The lecturer recommended that the essay include two case studies. Which verb form follows recommended in this clause?
items.explanation: After recommend, the subjunctive base form include is used in the that clause, while includes, included and including do not fit.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. Rising sea levels pose a serious threat to low-lying coastal cities. Which form of the word is needed after the adjective serious?
items.explanation: A noun is needed after the adjective serious, so threat is correct, while threaten, threatening and threatened are verb or adjective forms.
items.reference: PTE Academic Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary
